wages.text: Womack said workers’ rights should be strengthened so wages keep pace with living costs.
wages.quote: And we must strengthen workers’ rights so wages keep pace with the real cost of living.

housing.text: Womack called for expanding the affordable-housing supply by reducing construction costs.
housing.quote: We must expand the supply of affordable housing by reducing construction costs and opposing policies that trap families in long-term debt rather than building wealth.

schools.text: Womack pledged robust public-school funding and equitable resources for teachers and students.
schools.quote: I will advocate for robust public school funding, equitable resources for teachers and students, access to early childhood education, and affordable pathways to college and career training.

abortion.text: Womack called for protecting reproductive health-care access nationwide.
abortion.quote: We must allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices, cap out-of-pocket expenses, protect reproductive health care access nationwide, and invest in maternal health outcomes.

health.text: Womack supports strengthening the Affordable Care Act in the short term and moving toward Medicare for All.
health.quote: But in the long term, I do support a Medicare for All system so that everyone has access to healthcare, because people should not have to go bankrupt just because they get sick.

tax.text: Moore said keeping taxes low stimulates economic activity and increases revenue.
tax.quote: I believe, as a fiscal conservative, that by cutting taxes, by keeping taxes low, you spur economic activity, which will help the economy move along and thereby actually result in increased revenue.

housing.text: Moore voted for legislation intended to reduce regulatory barriers and accelerate home construction.
housing.quote: These housing reforms will help banks provide more construction loans that get shovels in the ground and opportunities for first-time homebuyers.

schools.text: Moore publicly defended expanding North Carolina's private-school voucher program.
schools.quote: During the pre-hearing news conference, House Speaker Tim Moore said the expanded voucher program will not undermine public schools.

safety.text: Moore called for policies providing law-enforcement officers with additional tools and training.
safety.quote: We must also advance policies that give them the tools, training, and respect they need to do their jobs and get home safely.

immigration.text: Moore praised military border enforcement and introduced legislation honoring personnel assigned to border operations.
immigration.quote: American troops at our southern border have bravely worked to stop the invasion of our country, one that threatened both our national security and our sovereignty.

guns.text: Moore helped enact the repeal of North Carolina's handgun purchase-permit requirement over the governor's veto.
guns.quote: have been long-standing goals of Second Amendment advocates in our state, and we have finally brought this legislation over the finish line.

abortion.text: Moore supported prohibiting most abortions after 12 weeks, with specified exceptions, and had previously supported a roughly six-week limit.
abortion.quote: The consensus position that we've developed, and I think I've been saying this now for quite a while, is around a 12-week period, with those exceptions built in for rape, incest, life of the mother and fetal abnormality

energy.text: Moore advocated expanding domestic energy production to reduce inflation and strengthen the economy.
energy.quote: If we can exploit and provide more energy, the resources that we have, that's going to do a lot to lower inflation and to really turn our economy around.

voting.text: Moore's campaign highlights enactment of voter-identification requirements as a leadership accomplishment.
voting.quote: Under his leadership, the state enforced voter ID protections, outlawed sanctuary cities, balanced the budget every year, and delivered the single largest personal income tax cut in state history.
